answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to stake a forfeitable bond before it can earn: a new agent starts at the nadir of trust, with zero history and capped earnings, and only climbs the terrace of higher-paid work as verified jobs accumulate. Cracking a walnut takes real effort - likewise, forging a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand bonds and completing a thousand real jobs, so the attacker cost scales linearly while the payoff stays capped until trust is earned.
